scope.note: All six runs are protocol pilots and are excluded from the later 20+20 statistical series; warm primes are also excluded from the pilot cold-versus-hit comparison.

findings.statement: The current NDDev fleet serializes this five-job workflow and queue time dominates end-to-end duration.
findings.evidence: NDDev maximum queue-to-start was 504000 ms cold and 568000 ms on the cache-hit pilot, versus 3000-5000 ms on GitHub-hosted pilots.

findings.statement: GitHub-hosted actions/cache is not the target local cache plane for NDDev workers.
findings.evidence: On NDDev, warm-hit elapsed time regressed for Bun, Docker, Python and Rust; Go improved only from 89946305332 ns to 85979166787 ns.

findings.statement: Disposable-runner uniqueness held across every NDDev pilot.
findings.evidence: Each NDDev run contained five distinct runner names and five distinct hashed machine identities; the postcondition contained zero registered runners, instances, leases or orphans.

findings.statement: The pilot is not a statistical baseline and does not satisfy the Phase 0 measurement gate.
findings.evidence: The required 20 cold and 20 cache-hit runs per environment have not yet been collected.
